title: Latency-driven runway and price sensitivity mapping
content:
High-level purpose:
Map headcount and payroll slope to latency SLA tiers and model price points. Goal: present a compact scenario sheet that shows how small changes in price / latency SLOs cascade to runway and hiring gates.

Summary table (headcount by org, baseline & two scenarios):
Row headers: Role / Q1-2026 baseline / Q2-2026 baseline / Q3-2026 baseline / Q4-2026 baseline / Q1-2027 baseline / Q1-2027 - latency-relax / Q1-2027 - aggressive-pricing
Engineering - serving-runtime, Devs: 28 / 30 / 32 / 34 / 36 / 34 / 38
SRE & Infra Ops: 9 / 10 / 10 / 11 / 12 / 10 / 14
Applied ML (model onboarding & evals): 6 / 7 / 8 / 9 / 10 / 9 / 11
Console & Product: 7 / 7 / 8 / 8 / 9 / 8 / 10
Developer Experience & SDKs: 4 / 4 / 5 / 5 / 6 / 5 / 6
Sales & Solutions Eng: 12 / 13 / 14 / 15 / 15 / 14 / 16
Customer Success & Support: 10 / 11 / 12 / 12 / 13 / 12 / 13
Finance, Legal, People: 6 / 6 / 6 / 6 / 7 / 6 / 7
Total headcount: 82 / 88 / 95 / 100 / 108 / 104 / 115

Assumptions (single-source-of-truth):
- Payroll blended cost per FTE (fully-burdened): Eng $190k, SRE $220k, ML $210k, Product/Console $160k, DX $150k, Sales/SE $170k, CS $120k, Ops $140k.
- Token mix and latency coupling: 60% short-chat flows (SLA 50-150ms), 30% medium generation (SLA 150-400ms), 10% long-form (SLA 400-1000ms).
- Latency-relax scenario reduces infra headcount need by ~10% across SRE/Infra and serving-runtime by allowing larger batching/k8s consolidation; risk: 4–7% QoE-driven revenue attrition for latency-sensitive customers.
- Aggressive-pricing scenario: +8% list price on hosted API (per-token), expected take-rate drop 6% but per-token revenue up net ~1.7% after elasticity; reduces required headcount growth (because additional revenue funds hires) but increases churn risk on price-sensitive accounts.

Scenario outputs (projected 12-month runway & margin effects):
Columns: Scenario / Projected ARR delta (12mo) / Gross margin change pct / Headcount delta / Runway change (months)
Baseline (no changes) / +$0 / 0.0% / +16 / 0 months
Latency-relax (deprioritize 50ms SLO) / -$2.4M / -3.2% / -4 / +1.8 months
Aggressive-pricing (8% price lift) / +$3.1M / +2.5% / +7 / -1.4 months
Combined (relax + pricing) / +$0.6M / -0.8% / +3 / +0.4 months

Per-token sensitivity grid (simplified):
Rows: Price delta / Volume elasticity assumed / Net revenue delta per 100M tokens / Impact on margin (bps)
-10% price / elasticity -0.9 / -$85k / -210 bps
-5% price / elasticity -0.7 / -$28k / -70 bps
0% price / elasticity -0.4 / $0 / 0 bps
+5% price / elasticity -0.3 / +$42k / +105 bps
+8% price / elasticity -0.25 / +$68k / +170 bps

Runway math notes (formulas visible in sheet):
- Runway delta = (cash buffer + scenario ARR delta * CAC-adjust / annual burn) converted to months.
- Annual burn = existing OPEX + incremental payroll from headcount delta.
- Payroll incremental = sum(FTE_delta * blended_FTE_cost) prorated to year.
- QoE attrition assumed to reduce gross ARR by % in latency-relax scenario (applied to top 200 customers weighted average).

Trigger rules (operational playbook entries):
- If MTD token volume drops >12% after price increase for 6 weeks -> revert price change on Tier-1 customers and roll back Sales commission holdback.
- If median p95 latency (hosted API) drifts above 350ms for >48 hours -> pause non-critical infra consolidations and re-open 3 hiring slots in SRE.
- If ARR delta from pricing > $1.5M sustained over 3 months -> accelerate hiring for Console/Product (+2 FTE) to capture product-led expansion.

Risks and mitigating controls:
- Elasticity estimates have low confidence on long-tail enterprise accounts -> mitigation: AB test on 30 customers before full roll.
- Latency QoE effect is non-linear for real-time integrations -> mitigation: prioritize regional routing fallbacks and issue a conservative latency SLA for top accounts.
- Headcount ramp friction -> mitigation: contractor bridge plan for critical infra roles (budget line item C-Contractors).

Action items / next steps (owner tags):
- Finance: produce detailed monthly cashflow + sensitivity by token volume (owner: Priya).
- SRE/Serving: produce microbenchmark showing cost saving per 10% infra consolidation (owner: Marcus Chen).
- Sales: selected account AB test plan for price lift (owner: Tomás Alvarez).
- Product: define feature gating to limit QoE regressions for top customers (owner: Aisha Patel).

Notes on provenance and data sources:
- Baseline payroll numbers pulled from payroll extract (payroll-export-2025Q3.csv).
- Volume and token mix come from product-analytics: token-mix-agg-v2 (internal BigQuery).

Sheet attachments / tabs in original workbook (for auditors):
- Tab: Assumptions (detail)
- Tab: HC by role (monthly)
- Tab: Price sensitivity grid (token buckets)
- Tab: Cashflow + runway calculation
- Tab: AB test roster and outcomes

Quick read TL;DR (one-liner):
Small latency tradeoffs can materially lengthen runway at the expense of near-term ARR; a modest price lift offsets much of that loss but requires cautious AB testing and targeted mitigations for latency-sensitive customers.
